Aybak ruled from Lahore; Delhi became the sultanate's capital under Iltutmish (r. 1211–1236). 'Capital since 1206' is an anachronism.
findings.old: صارت عاصمة سلاطين دلهي منذ 1206 م، فبنوا
findings.fix: صارت عاصمة سلاطين دلهي في عهد إيلتتمش (نحو 1211 م) بعد أن كان أيبك يحكم من لاهور، فبنوا
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mamluk_dynasty_(Delhi) — Aibak's capital Lahore; Iltutmish shifted the capital to Delhi

findings.issue: Aybak is not known to have formally assumed the title sultan (he used malik/sipahsalar, struck no coins in his name); stating he 'declared himself sultan' is overstated.

findings.fix: استقل القائد قطب الدين أيبك بالحكم بعد مقتل سيده محمد الغوري

findings.issue: Akbar's interfaith debates were held in the Ibadat Khana (1575), not the Diwan-i-Khas; identifying the Diwan-i-Khas as the debate hall is a popular misattribution.
findings.old: ودار «ديوان خاص» التي كان أكبر يجالس فيها العلماء من الأديان المختلفة
findings.fix: و«عبادت خانه» (دار العبادة) التي كان أكبر يجالس فيها العلماء من الأديان المختلفة
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibadat_Khana — 'meeting house built in 1575 by Akbar at Fatehpur Sikri to gather spiritual leaders of different religions'

findings.issue: Chronology: the large Ottoman musketeer contingent (~900 men) reached Imam Ahmad only in 1542, in response to the Portuguese expedition; his 1529–1541 conquests were made with a mostly local army with a small matchlock contingent.
findings.fix: وكان في جيشه عدد قليل من حملة البنادق، ثم أمدّه العثمانيون بنحو تسعمئة منهم سنة 1542 م.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian%E2%80%93Adal_War ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_ibn_Ibrahim_al-Ghazi (Ottoman reinforcement of 900 musketeers after Portuguese arrival)

findings.issue: Birthplace disputed: Wikipedia states Rumi was born in Wakhsh (in the province of Balkh, now Tajikistan), with the city of Balkh the traditional account. Stated as certain.

findings.fix: وُلد في إقليم بلخ وعاش في قونية
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rumi — 'born in Wakhsh, a village ... in present-day Tajikistan ... Wakhsh belonged to the larger province of Balkh'

findings.issue: Same disputed birthplace stated as certain in the section text.

findings.issue: The Delhi massacre (22 March 1739) is understated as 'large numbers'; standard accounts give c. 20,000–30,000 dead in one day, triggered by riots after a rumour of Nader's death. Neutral, factual figures should be given.
findings.old: فلما قُتل بعض جنوده في اضطرابات أمر بقتل أعداد كبيرة من أهلها
findings.fix: فلما قُتل بعض جنوده في اضطرابات أثارتها شائعة موته أمر في 22 مارس 1739 م بقتل أهلها، فقُتل نحو عشرين إلى ثلاثين ألفًا بحسب أكثر التقديرات

findings.issue: Ghazni was already the seat of Alp-Tegin's successors from 962; Sebüktigin took power there in 977 rather than 'adopting it as seat' that year.

findings.fix: تولى الحكم فيها القائد التركي سبكتكين سنة 977 م
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghazni ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabuktigin (Alp-Tegin seized Ghazni 962; Sebüktigin succeeded 977)

findings.issue: Johor was founded by one son, Alauddin Riayat Shah II (c. 1528); another son founded Perak. 'Sons founded Johor' is imprecise.
